claims: The Michigan Fab Five were a 1991 University of Michigan men's basketball recruiting class.
The Michigan Fab Five consisted of Chris Webber, Jalen Rose, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King, and Ray Jackson.
The Michigan Fab Five were the first NCAA team to start five freshmen.
The Michigan Fab Five reached NCAA championship games in 1992 and 1993.
The Fab Five led Michigan to the 1992 NCAA championship game.
Michigan lost to Duke 71-51 in the 1992 NCAA championship game.
The Fab Five led Michigan to the 1993 NCAA championship game.
Michigan lost to North Carolina 77-71 in the 1993 NCAA championship game.
The Fab Five introduced baggy shorts and black socks in basketball fashion.
Booster Ed Martin made illegal payments to several players including Chris Webber.
Michigan vacated its 1992 and 1993 Final Four appearances.
Juwan Howard coached Michigan from 2019 to 2024.
The Fab Five members appeared for an alternate broadcast during the 2026 NCAA tournament
